result.reason: Both items together constitute Rav Naḥman's ruling that witnesses who claim their signed document was an amana or moda'ah are not believed — exactly the content described in the 'Rav Nachman: No Retract' prose section.
The passage directly articulates the peh vs. shtar doctrine — oral testimony cannot override a document but one document can override another — which is precisely what section 0's prose discusses.

Both items discuss the Rav Naḥman / Mar bar Rav Ashi dispute about whether witnesses who claim their signed document was an amana or moda'ah are deemed credible — exactly the content the 'Amana vs. Moda'ah Ethics' prose analyzes in detail.

The passage presents the Gemara's 'pishita' (obvious) objection that since the husband has legal rights to the produce (peirot), his use of the land cannot establish chazaka — exactly the content described in the 'No Chazaka Despite Peirot' section's prose.

Both items directly address the 'din u-devarim ein li bi-nechasayich' waiver formulation and the baraita challenging its legal effectiveness, which is precisely what the 'Waiver Before Marriage' prose discusses.

Both items directly present the school of Rabbi Yannai's answer (the mishna speaks of a waiver written during erusin) and Rav Kahana's principle about pre-emptive renunciation of a future rabbinic benefit, which is precisely what the 'Rav Kahana Nachalah' prose section explains and contextualizes.

The passage directly presents Rav Huna's ruling about a woman waiving mezonot in exchange for keeping her earnings, which is precisely the content the 'Aikkar Mezonot' prose discusses as the identification of 'ke-gone zo' and the foundational ruling for that section's analysis.

The passage directly discusses the Gemara's pivot from chazaka to rayah (proof via shtar) and the wife's counter-claim of 'nachat ruach asiti le-ba'ali,' which is precisely what the 'Nachat Ruach Claim' section's prose describes.

All three items form a continuous unit: item 1 cites the Mishnah about purchasing from husband then wife (nachat ruach), and items 2-3 give Rabba bar Rav Huna's qualification about the three fields — this entire exchange is precisely what heading 0 ('Lien Waiver Invalid') describes in its prose, including the nachat ruach defense and the three ketubah fields context, whereas heading 1 ('Three Fields of Ketubah') describes the limiting function of 'these three fields' (le-mautei mai) which is the next section's topic.

The passage discusses exactly what 'these three fields' excludes (le-mautei mai), concluding that excluding other property would only strengthen the enmity argument, which matches the 'Selling Milog Valid' section's prose about this precise Gemara passage.
